site.heroDescription: Christ Episcopal Church in Coronado, California — a vibrant, worshiping, beachside community shaped by prayer, fellowship, and service.

ministryProfiles.title: What we hope for in our next rector.
ministryProfiles.content: We need a collaborative leader who listens well, builds trust, and works closely with vestry, lay leaders, school, and staff. Administrative skill and wise stewardship are essential, as is adaptability in a changing Church. Above all, we seek a rector grounded in prayer and emotional maturity—someone who will help us grow as a supportive community led by the Holy Spirit and rooted in faith, hope, and love.

ministryProfiles.title: Supporting diverse worship traditions
ministryProfiles.content: Christ Church welcomes all of God's children with hope and openness as we prepare for the future. We support worship and pastoral care through dedicated parishioners, strengthened by clergy guidance, and we offer both Rite I and Rite II so people can worship in the tradition that best nourishes them.

ministryProfiles.title: Growing engagement and community visibility
ministryProfiles.content: We grow engagement through active ministries and committees, intentionally inviting new voices into shared leadership and discernment. We also work to be visible in the wider community, so our neighbors know who we are and how we seek to follow Jesus. Our partnership with Christ Church Day School is a treasured part of our identity, and we are strengthening youth formation through Godly Play, fellowship, and meaningful learning.

ministryProfiles.title: Who will we call as our next rector?
ministryProfiles.content: We hope to call a leader who embodies Christ's love with humility, compassion, and spiritual depth. Essential gifts include strong pastoral presence, excellent liturgical leadership, and preaching that connects the Gospel to everyday life with warmth and clarity. We value someone who helps newcomers feel truly welcome and who nurtures long-time members with care, especially in seasons of joy, grief, and transition.

ministryProfiles.title: Stewarding our campus and diocesan partnerships
ministryProfiles.content: We care for our 130-year-old campus as a gift entrusted to us, planning responsibly for maintenance and future needs. Finally, we seek deeper relationships across the Diocese, especially with parishes serving immigrant communities, so we can stand with those most in need.

ministryProfiles.title: Serving beyond our parish
ministryProfiles.content: Our Service Ministry helps our parish live out a faith that is truly active and visible. James 2:17 says, "So also faith by itself, if it does not have works, is dead." Guided by that call, we raise funds for Vida Joven orphanages in Mexico through our annual Cinco de Mayo dinner. We also provide backpacks and school supplies for children at the start of the school year.

ministryProfiles.title: Caring for our neighbors
ministryProfiles.content: In recent years, we revived a longtime tradition of offering practical care to neighbors experiencing homelessness by equipping parishioners with small gift bags of essentials to share with dignity and kindness. Our Thrift Shop further extends this outreach. It is a true community ministry, with volunteers and donors from well beyond our congregation.

ministryProfiles.title: Peace & Justice ministry
ministryProfiles.content: We stay connected and engaged through our weekly newsletter, Grace Notes, which highlights opportunities to serve in the wider community. In addition, our Peace & Justice Committee supports education and advocacy on issues such as housing, ocean pollution, immigration, and LGBTQ protections and rights, helping us respond thoughtfully and faithfully to our neighbors' needs.

ministryProfiles.title: Sacred Ground & community organizing
ministryProfiles.content: In the past five years, one of our most significant new ministries has been the formation of our Peace & Justice Committee. During COVID, parishioners participated in the Episcopal Church's Sacred Ground program, which deepened our commitment to faithful action and honest conversation. From that work, we sensed a call to engage issues affecting our neighbors, and we joined the San Diego Organizing Project (SDOP), a non-partisan, multi-faith network. Through listening and discernment, we focused first on housing, homelessness, and ocean pollution, supporting efforts such as renter protections, housing initiatives, and practical support for the unhoused.

ministryProfiles.title: Faithful accompaniment for migrants
ministryProfiles.content: More recently, we have felt a clear call toward immigration and refugee support. We have hosted Home Meetings, participated in forums and rallies, and held discussions on issues including refugee resettlement. In collaboration with Our Lady of Guadalupe Church and SDOP, we now support the FAITH program (Faithful Accompaniment in Trust & Hope), offering moral and prayerful presence for migrants at court hearings and related sites.

ministryProfiles.title: Worship, prayer, and community life
ministryProfiles.content: Christ Church is a loving, Spirit-filled community grounded in worship, prayer, and relationships. We are nourished through thoughtful liturgy, beautiful music, and gathering at the Lord's Table. Fellowship also matters to us: shared meals and parish gatherings deepen connection and remind us we do not walk alone. We care for one another's spiritual, emotional, and physical well-being through formation, prayer, and community life.

ministryProfiles.title: Formation and hospitality
ministryProfiles.content: Weekly Men's Bible Study and lay-led Evening Prayer offer regular opportunities for scripture, reflection, and shared intercession. We also support health of mind and body through offerings such as an on-site yoga class held twice a month.

ministryProfiles.title: Hospitality and service
ministryProfiles.content: Beyond our parish, we extend care through hospitality by opening our facilities to youth events, scouting groups, arts performances, fundraisers, and Alcoholics Anonymous meetings. Our all-volunteer Thrift Shop is a ministry of compassion that provides affordable, high-quality goods and distributes over $100,000 annually to ministries locally and throughout the wider Church.

ministryProfiles.title: Our parish-school partnership
ministryProfiles.content: Our partnership with Christ Church Day School is a treasured and defining part of our parish identity. For 70 years, we have shared our campus, our worship life, and our commitment to Christian formation with students and families who bring energy, diversity, and joy to our community. We believe this partnership strengthens both church and school. Students participate in weekly chapels, building early connections to Episcopal worship and tradition.

ministryProfiles.title: Building relationships across generations
ministryProfiles.content: Parents and faculty often join parish events, deepening relationships across generations. Service projects unite school families and parishioners in common mission. Our Day School chaplain serves both communities, weaving together formation, pastoral care, and spiritual nurture.

ministryProfiles.title: Caring for our campus
ministryProfiles.content: We care for our 130-year-old campus as a gift entrusted to us by past generations and held in trust for those to come. As we plan responsibly for maintenance, growth, and future needs, we do so knowing that this sacred space serves not only Sunday worship but also the daily formation of young hearts and minds throughout the week.

ministryProfiles.title: Ministry as Christ's hands and feet
ministryProfiles.content: We invite everyone to share in ministry as we seek to be Christ's "hands and feet" in the world. Parishioners serve our neighbors through outreach that meets real needs with dignity and care. We support St. Mark's kitchen and prepare "Blessings in a Bag" with snacks, water, and handmade hats, gloves, or scarves to offer those living on the streets. These remind our neighbors that they are seen and loved by God the Father, Son, and Spirit.

ministryProfiles.title: Prayer and belonging for all
ministryProfiles.content: We also create space for prayer and belonging. Our mid-week, lay-led Evening Prayer service is intentionally welcoming and nonjudgmental, with opportunities for people to speak names and concerns aloud. In seasons like Lent, we gather for Stations of the Cross and a lecture series, sharing a simple meal and deepening fellowship.

ministryProfiles.title: Witnessing to inclusive love
ministryProfiles.content: Our congregation participates in the San Diego Pride celebration alongside others in the Diocese, praying at the Cathedral and witnessing to God's inclusive love. We support Vida Joven orphanages in Mexico through fundraising that helps provide food and care.

ministryProfiles.title: Standing with migrants in court
ministryProfiles.content: Through our Peace and Justice Ministry, we educate ourselves about suffering at the border and offer prayerful presence for those facing immigration court proceedings, standing as compassionate witnesses and reminding people they are not alone.

ministryProfiles.title: The Thrift Shop ministry
ministryProfiles.content: Our volunteer-run Thrift Shop is another vital ministry. It offers affordable clothing and household goods to the larger community while generating annual support for staff, parish ministries, local organizations, and scholarships. It is entirely staffed by volunteers and is known as a place of warmth, generosity, and good humor.

ministryProfiles.title: Growing youth formation
ministryProfiles.content: We are encouraged by new life in our ministries: our youth programs are rebuilding with the hiring of Leighton Jones, our new Youth Minister and Day School chaplain. We are nurturing the next generation through thoughtful Christian formation that invites wonder, questions, and belonging.

ministryProfiles.title: Our vision for youth and families
ministryProfiles.content:
• Regular Sunday School and youth gatherings that build friendships rooted in faith
  • Godly Play sessions that help children encounter scripture through story and wonder
  • Service opportunities that connect young people to Christ's mission in the world
  • Intergenerational worship and fellowship that strengthens the whole parish family
  • Deepening partnerships with Christ Church Day School for shared formation and worship
  • Creating space where young people feel genuinely seen, heard, and valued
  • Supporting parents and families as they nurture faith at home

index.title: Welcome
index.description: Christ Church Coronado seeks a compassionate rector to lead our friendly Episcopal community in worship, service, and faith formation.

sections.heading: Welcome to Christ Church
content: We are a friendly, inclusive Episcopal community in Coronado, California. Our parish is home to over 200 members from all walks of life, including many military families. We value tradition, thoughtful worship, and caring for one another as our God cares for us. Our motto "Bridging Love and Service" reflects our desire to mimic Christ by growing a spiritual community in harmony with our surrounding secular community.

Christ Church Day School is one of our largest bridges. Founded in 1957, it is the only Episcopal elementary school in the Diocese of San Diego. We are committed to its future and to Christian education for all ages.

We seek an experienced leader who will work collaboratively with vestry, lay leaders, school, and staff. We welcome all people and look forward to meeting our next rector. If you feel called, we hope to hear from you.
✞ The People of Christ Church

sections.heading: Our Hopes for Our Next Rector
content: We hope to call a leader who embodies Christ's love with humility, compassion, and spiritual depth. Essential gifts include strong pastoral presence, excellent liturgical leadership, and preaching that connects the Gospel to everyday life with warmth and clarity. We value someone who helps newcomers feel truly welcome and who nurtures long-time members with care, especially in seasons of joy, grief, and transition.
Some characteristics of our next rector:

• Discovering new bridges for us in service and outreach
  • Lead us in meaningful service and outreach
  • Strengthen youth and family ministries
  • Deepen our relationship with the Day School
  • Welcome new members and nurture spiritual growth to increase membership
  • Support small groups and ongoing formation
  • Provide compassionate care in all seasons of life
  • Demonstrate strong administrative leadership and staff management skills

family.title: A Welcoming Parish Family
family.description: Experience the warmth and community of Christ Church Coronado. We are a family united in faith, worship, and service.

sections.heading: United in faith, worship, and service
content: Christ Church Coronado is more than just a place to attend church—it’s a family rooted in Christ.
With a vibrant community of over 200 members, we come together to worship, care for one another, and serve God beyond our walls.
Our parish brings together people at every stage of life: young children growing their faith through Godly Play, Parish Day School
families practicing Christian values in their lives, adults living their faith through service ministries, and longtime members

who share wisdom and spiritual depth to all.

We are honored to include military families, newcomers, lifelong Coronado residents,
and everyone in between. Whether you’re visiting for the first time or have called this community home for years, you are
welcome here. Together, we seek the presence of the Holy Spirit through meaningful worship, genuine fellowship,
and a shared commitment to serving one another and our neighbors.

sections.heading: Where everyone finds a place
content: Our parish flourishes because of the many gifts shared by our family. Whether leading worship, serving coffee, volunteering
at the Thrift Shop, supporting our youth groups, or teaching in our Day School, each of us plays a meaningful part in God’s work.

We celebrate milestones together—baptisms and confirmations, weddings and anniversaries. We also walk alongside one another through life's challenges, offering pastoral care and prayerful presence in times of grief, loss, and transition.

In our shared meals, community events, and worship services, we experience the joy of belonging. We are a community grounded in prayer, nourished by the Eucharist, and sent forth to live out our faith in the wider world.

worship.title: Worship
worship.description: Join us for traditional Episcopal worship at Christ Church Coronado. Sundays at 8am (Rite I) and 10am (Rite II with choir).

sections.heading: Prayer, Eucharist, and fellowship
content: At Christ Church Coronado, worship is at the heart of who we are. We are a friendly,
inclusive community where everyone is invited to encounter God through prayer, sacrament, and fellowship.
All are welcome at Christ's table. Whether they are new, returning, or seeking, they are invited to join us.
Weekly Worship Schedule:
<ul class='list-disc list-inside'>
• Sunday 8:00 am – Holy Eucharist (Rite I)
• Sunday 10:00 am – Holy Eucharist (Rite II, choir & organ)
• Tuesday 8:00 am – Holy Eucharist (Rite II, Day School Chapel)
• Thursday 8:00 am – Morning Prayer (with Class Chaplains)
• Wednesday 5:30 pm – Evening Prayer (lay led)
Most of our members value our traditional faith, but some would like more variety in worship, prayers, and music.
As we look to the future, we seek to honor the liturgical beauty that nourishes us while remaining open to new expressions of praise and prayer.

youth_family.title: Youth & Family
youth_family.description: Youth and family ministry at Christ Church Coronado includes Sunday School, Kids Praise choir, and Camp Create summer VBS.

sections.heading: Growing in faith together
content: We welcome children, teens, and families to grow in faith together.
Worship at Christ Church is wiggle-friendly!
Families are always welcome to worship together during Sunday services.
Children’s worship materials are available in the first pew
prayground
to help engage young hearts and minds.
Our youth ministries include:
<ul class='list-disc list-inside'>
• Weekly Godly Play story circles and Youth Group every other Sunday.
• Participation in diocesan children and youth events nurturing a broader faith community.
• Summer Vacation Bible School.
• Intergenerational worship, events, and programming.
• Opportunities to serve Sunday mornings and in Outreach.

service_ministry.title: Service Ministry
service_ministry.description: Christ Church Coronado's service ministry includes refugee support, food drives, and partnerships with St. Mark's and SDOP.

sections.heading: Bridging love and service
content: <div class='flex-content'>
<div class='flex-1'>
Our Service Ministry helps our parish live an active, visible faith. Meeting monthly, this core group of volunteers
plans outreach efforts for the church community. Our parish community not only provides financial support as it offers
hands-on opportunities, allowing for involvement in our spiritual call to help others. While some activities are held at
church, others involve heading over the bridge to <a href='https://stmarks-cityheights.org/' target='_blank'
rel='noopener noreferrer' class='link'>St. Mark's and
target='_blank' rel='noopener noreferrer' class='link'>St. Luke's parishes to provide support for the unhoused and those in need.
As James 2:17 reminds us, "faith without works is dead". Guided by that call, we raise funds for
Vida Joven
through our annual festive Cinco de Mayo dinner, which provides shelter for orphans in Tijuana and Northern Mexico.
The Backpack Drive provides over 200 backpacks filled with school supplies for children, and our Thanksgiving Drive
works with Christ Church Day School to collect food and financial donations to provide food for 200 families.
We share the joy of Advent by providing Christmas gifts for the <a href='https://episcopalcommunityservices.org/'
target='_blank' rel='noopener noreferrer' class='link'>Episcopal Community Services Head Start programs.
And our Lenten Drive annually supports causes the Service Ministry team identifies to serve those in need.
This year we are assisting RefugeeNet to send children to summer swim lessons and robotics camp.
In recent years, we revived "Blessings in a Bag", a tradition of practical care for neighbors experiencing homelessness
by equipping parishioners with small gift bags of food and essentials to share with dignity and kindness.
Our Thrift Shop, by raising over $100,000 per year, extends this outreach as a community ministry, supported by
volunteers and donors beyond our congregation. Ongoing, Christ Church partners with St. Mark's to support their
Food Pantry, now serving 400 families weekly.

day_school.description: Christ Church Day School is a thriving JK-8 Episcopal school in Coronado, serving 130 students with small classes since 1957.

sections.heading: A thriving Episcopal school in the heart of Coronado
content: <div class='flex-content'>
<div class='flex-1'>
Christ Church Day School
(CCDS) is a vital mission of Christ Church, serving JK–8th grade with 130 students in small classes.
Founded in 1957, CCDS provides quality education grounded in Christian values.
It is accredited by the <a href='https://acswasc.org/' target='blank' rel='noopener'
class='link'>Western Association of Schools and Colleges (WASC) and a member of the
<a href='https://www.episcopalschools.org/' target='blank' rel='noopener'
class='link'>National Association of Episcopal Schools (NAES)
<div class='stats-grid'>

Enrollment
130 students, JK–8

Class sizes
Small (about 14–16)

Founded
1957
Students receive rich specialty programs including Spanish, Music, Physical Education, Art, and Spiritual Nurture.
CCDS hosts twice-weekly all-school chapels with Eucharist on Tuesdays and Morning Prayer on Thursdays.
CCDS keeps the campus alive and vibrant with open houses, back-to-school events, an annual Harvest Festival,
movie nights on the lawn, music and talent performances, family nights, pet blessings, Scholastic Book Fairs,
and end-of-year celebrations. The school partners frequently with the church on service projects,
including our annual Spaghetti Dinner and Thanksgiving Food Drive.
Learn more at ccds.org.

thrift_shop.title: Thrift Shop
thrift_shop.description: Christ Church Thrift Shop has served Coronado for 70+ years, raising over $100,000 annually for parish ministries and outreach.

sections.heading: Joining God's work in the world
content: <div class='flex-content'>
<div class='flex-1'>
One of the most significant and impactful ministries of Christ Church is our Thrift Shop.
In operation for over 75 years, it is managed and staffed entirely by nearly 50 volunteers from
Christ Church and the surrounding community. All proceeds support a wide range of parish activities
and outreach efforts at the diocesan, national, and international levels. In 2025 alone, over $100,000
in funds were provided to worthwhile ministries, including <a href='https://ccds.org'
target='_blank' rel='noopener noreferrer' class='link'>Christ Church Day School, the
San Diego Food Bank,
World Central Kitchen,
PAWS
(our local animal welfare group), <a href='https://vjkids.org/' target='_blank' rel='noopener noreferrer'
class='link'>Vida Joven (a foundation that supports orphanages in Mexico),
target='_blank' rel='noopener noreferrer' class='link'>The Episcopal Refugee Network, and various other projects
of The Episcopal Diocese of San Diego.
Beyond its vital financial outreach, the Thrift Shop provides help to low-income families by offering quality merchandise at
very low cost. It also creates fellowship for volunteers and shoppers who've developed relationships over the years. The shop
is open for sales and donations on Tuesday through Saturday, 10 am to 1 pm.
The Thrift Shop embodies our call to service in tangible, practical ways, connecting commerce with compassion and stewardship with generosity.

music_ministry.title: Music Ministry
music_ministry.description: Music ministry is central to worship at Christ Church Coronado, featuring our choir, organ, and sacred music traditions.

sections.heading: Music at Christ Church
content: <div class='flex-content'>
<div class='flex-1'>
For centuries, music has been closely connected with faith
and worship. At Christ Church, singing, hymns, and the organ continue this long
tradition of Anglican worship, inviting everyone to take part. Music has a unique
power: it lifts the words of the liturgy, highlights important moments in the
service, and brings depth and beauty that spoken words alone cannot always express.
Through psalms, hymns, and choral music, the congregation shares in prayer and
praise together.
<div class='flex-1'>
<div class='video-container'>
<video width='100%' height='auto' controls playsinline preload='metadata'>
<source src='assets/Song1-1.mp4' type='video/mp4'>
Your browser does not support HTML5 video playback.
</video>
Music also draws people together. When voices join in song,
a sense of unity and encouragement is created, strengthening both the community
and the faith of each individual. Sacred music expresses the wide range of
emotions found in worship—joy, sorrow, thanksgiving, and hope—and offers a way
to respond to God in a universal language understood by all.
At Christ Church, music is therefore more than a background to worship—
it is an essential part of it. Whether through the choir, the organ, or the
congregation singing as one, music enriches the liturgy, marks important
moments of prayer and praise, and helps us experience God’s presence and
love in a meaningful way.

rectory.title: The Rectory
rectory.description: The Rectory at Christ Church Coronado is the home of our rector, a central part of parish life and ministry.

sections.heading: A home for our rector
content: Christ Church Coronado is blessed to own a rectory available for the rector and their family. The rectory is a spacious two-story home featuring three bedrooms, a living room, den, dining room, an updated kitchen, a garage, and a comfortable patio area in the backyard.

Located approximately seven blocks from the church, the home is close enough for a pleasant walk or an easy bike ride to the parish campus. This convenient proximity allows for easy accessibility to parish activities and ministries while providing a peaceful residential setting for our rector and their family.

The Rectory at Christ Church Coronado serves as more than just a residence—it is a place where our spiritual leader lives, serves, and builds meaningful relationships with our parish community. From pastoral visits and counseling to hosting parish gatherings and welcoming visitors, the Rectory is central to the life and ministry of Christ Church.

We invite our next rector to make this home their own, and to use it as a base from which to shepherd our flock, nurture our faith community, and continue the rich tradition of Christ Church Coronado.
